note.note:
Subjective:
- Patient presents with lower abdominal pain of 3 days duration, progressively worsening in intensity.
- Pain described as sharp, localized to the right lower quadrant.
- Associated symptoms include nausea and low-grade fever.
- No history of similar episodes in the past.
- No reported bowel or urinary symptoms.
- Past medical history: none reported.
- Medications: none reported.
- Allergies: none reported.
- Social history: not provided.

Objective:
- Physical examination reveals tenderness and guarding in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen.
- Mild rebound tenderness noted.
- Vital signs show low-grade fever (temperature not specified).
- Other systemic examinations unremarkable.
- Investigations: none reported in transcript.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Abdominal pain:
   - Assessment: Likely acute appendicitis.
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with transcript):
     • Acute appendicitis (most likely).
     • Ovarian cyst rupture.
     • Mesenteric adenitis.
     • Urinary tract infection.
   - Investigations planned:
     • Abdominal ultrasound.
     • Complete blood count (CBC) to assess for leukocytosis.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Initiate pain management.
     • Recommend NPO status pending surgical evaluation.
   - Relevant referrals:
     • Surgical consult.

Quality checks:
- Allergies and medications reconciliation missing but clinically expected.
- No internal conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality is clear and audible.
